blocks.content: Course: Rapid Build With Claude Code

Here is something I see developers skip constantly: they open a design tool before they have decided what the product looks like. Then they spend two hours adjusting colors, changing their mind about fonts, and wondering why nothing feels cohesive.

Brand guidelines fix this. When you define every visual decision in a document before opening Figma, Framer, or a code editor - you never have to make those decisions again mid-project. Every design and code choice has an answer: check the guidelines.

For SpeedBlip, I locked the brand before writing a single line of code. That meant when Claude Code was building the landing page, it had exact hex values, font names, border-radius rules, and glassmorphism specs. There was no ambiguity.
The result: the app looks cohesive because every component was built from the same spec, not from gut feeling at the moment.
